userStories.title: Edge calibration service: detect MeasureCard, rectify perspective, persist px-per-inch
userStories.description: As the platform, given a 'measurement' photo I need a deterministic CV pass that finds the four card fiducials, computes a homography that rectifies the photo to a true top-down plane, derives pixels-per-inch, and persists that calibration — the foundation every measurement (auto or manual) is computed from. Server-side so iOS, web, and Android all share ONE implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/flipdesk/measure/calibrate {photoId}: loads the photo (signed, tenant-scoped via owner-verified parent item — tenant-isolation skill), detects the ArUco markers, identifies card version from the id set, computes the homography from the four marker centers to the known 6x4in rectangle, derives px-per-inch on the rectified plane, and returns {cardVersion, ppi, homography, quality}

Quality gates return actionable errors, not garbage numbers: fewer than 4 markers found (card not fully visible), min marker size < 40px (move camera closer), blur metric below threshold (photo too blurry), homography reprojection residual above threshold (card bent or photo too angled) — each with a user-facing remediation string

Calibration persists on the item_photos row (new nullable jsonb column, e.g. measure_calibration: {v, cardVersion, ppi, homography, quality, computedAt}) via a US-1108-triple migration, so re-opening the editor never re-runs detection

Implementation: ArUco detection + homography inside the existing Deno edge container (opencv WASM or a pure-TS ArUco port validated against OpenCV outputs); if WASM proves unworkable, a minimal Python/OpenCV sidecar container on Coolify behind the same route is the sanctioned fallback (document the choice in the code)

Deterministic test fixtures: >= 6 synthetic renders of the card geometry (straight-on, 15deg tilt, 30deg tilt, small-in-frame, one marker occluded, blurred) with known ground truth; calibrate must recover ppi within 1% on the passing cases and emit the RIGHT error on the failing ones
Endpoint registered in the tenant-isolation test suite (new-route rule)
userStories.notes: The homography is the whole ballgame for accuracy: it converts a slightly-angled photo from an error source into a solved problem. All downstream pixel math (auto landmarks AND the manual editor) happens in RECTIFIED coordinates. Raw photos stay untouched — rectification is a coordinate transform, not a rewrite of the stored image. BUILT 2026-07-03: pure-TS card-tuned detector (lib/measure-detect.ts — adaptive threshold via integral image, CC labeling, hull->quad, canonical unwarp + bit decode across 4 rotations, 16-corner least-squares DLT homography with normalization) — NO WASM/sidecar needed; CI validates against REAL OpenCV detections on 6 generated fixtures (scripts/generate-measure-fixtures.py; ids match, centers within 3px incl. 30deg tilt, ppi within 2%). Route POST /api/flipdesk/measure/calibrate (auth+gate+workspace+15/min limiter), tenant-scoped via inventory_items!inner, downloadItemPhoto helper, cached via item_photos.measure_calibration (migration 00347, HELD), downscale + homography rescale to original px. Calibration is NOT a billed AI action (source-guarded).

userStories.title: Auto measurement extraction: garment-class schema + AI landmark proposal + deterministic refinement
userStories.description: As a reseller, once my measurement photo is calibrated, GradeThread should pull the actual measurements out automatically: pit-to-pit, length, sleeve, waist, inseam, rise — whichever apply to the garment class — with per-measurement confidence, so most items need zero manual measuring.
acceptanceCriteria: A per-garment-class measurement schema module (shared constant, mirrored web/edge/iOS like the photo vocabulary): tops = chest/pit-to-pit, length, shoulder, sleeve; bottoms = waist, inseam, rise, hem/leg opening; dresses/outerwear/shoes each get their own set — this schema also drives which fields the editor (next story) renders

POST /api/flipdesk/measure/extract {photoId}: on the RECTIFIED image, Claude Vision proposes each measurement's two endpoints as NORMALIZED coordinates constrained by garment class (the existing AI-extraction pass supplies the class); a deterministic refinement step snaps each proposed endpoint to the nearest garment edge (contour/gradient search within a small window) — the VLM proposes, classical CV decides (VLMs alone are not pixel-accurate)
Each measurement returns {name, endpoints, inches, confidence}; inches = rectified pixel distance / ppi, rounded to 0.25in

Results write to item.measurements (existing jsonb consumed by the US-1450 publish aspects) plus a parallel measurement_sources provenance map (ai_measured), NEVER overwriting a manual entry — same fill-only provenance rules as reverseColumnAspects / SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md

Plausibility guard: compare extracted values against size-tag priors (existing size column; e.g. a mens L top with pit-to-pit outside 20-26in) — out-of-band measurements are flagged needs-review-style and surfaced in the editor rather than silently saved

Extraction is a billed AI ACTION: the endpoint reserves atomically via reserve_ai_action BEFORE the vision call (refund on failure — same reserve/refund contract as generation) and logs spend to ai_enrichment_log; one action covers the whole per-item extraction (all measurements in one prompt); calibrate (pure CV, no model call) is NOT billed
Deno tests: schema module; snapping function on synthetic edges; plausibility guard bands; provenance fill-only rules
userStories.notes: Designed to be WRONG sometimes and cheaply corrected: everything lands in the overlay editor pre-seeded, and every manual correction becomes telemetry for a future trained landmark model (eval-harness story). AutoLister integration: when a batch item has a calibrated measurement photo, run extract during generation so drafts arrive measured. Billing decision (2026-07-03): photo-measurement extraction counts toward the monthly AI-action allotment; deterministic calibration does not. BUILT 2026-07-03: NO new migration/column — provenance rides the EXISTING inventory_items.ai_field_sources with the measurements.<key> convention the MeasurementForm already badges (fill-only rules identical to the story: seller values never overwritten, AI refreshes AI, blanks fill). Schema module = existing MEASUREMENT_TEMPLATES/measurementGroupFor mirrored to edge (byte-equality test). lib/measure-extract.ts: one vision call proposes normalized endpoints per class field, deterministic gradient snap along the measurement axis (noise-floored), inches via the US-1572 homography, size-narrowed plausibility bands. Route POST /api/flipdesk/measure/extract: calibration required, checkQuota + withAiAction (ONE billed action; calibrate stays free — source-guard test), ai_enrichment_log spend row. Edge suite 2596/0.

userStories.title: Measurement overlay editor (web): review, drag-adjust, and save calibrated measurements
userStories.description: As a reseller, I review the auto-extracted measurements on an interactive overlay: the rectified photo with each measurement drawn as a draggable line and a live inch readout. I nudge endpoints, add missing measurements, delete wrong ones, and save. If the auto pass failed, I can still place every line manually — the calibration alone makes manual measuring a 10-second job.
acceptanceCriteria: Composer + item canvas gain a Measurements panel: when a calibrated measurement photo exists, it renders the rectified photo on a canvas with each schema measurement as a colored line with draggable endpoints and a live value chip (inches, 0.25 steps, unit pref respected via useMeasurementPrefs)

Pre-seeded from the extract output when present; a bare calibrated photo (no extract, or extract failed) starts with schema-default line placements the user drags into position — the editor NEVER requires the auto pass
Low-confidence / plausibility-flagged measurements render visually distinct (amber) so review attention goes to the right lines
Save writes item.measurements + measurement_sources=manual for touched entries (untouched ai_measured entries keep their provenance) and invalidates the items_full / item queries
The existing manual measurement-form remains for items with NO measurement photo — the overlay editor augments, never gates, measurement entry
vitest: endpoint-drag math (pixel to inch via ppi), provenance rules on save, unit conversion display
userStories.notes: Render in rectified coordinate space (apply the stored homography via canvas transform). Keep the editor logic in pure functions (hit-testing, px-to-inch) so the iOS/Android ports share the math by spec, not copy-paste drift. Mind the composer EMPTY_PHOTOS stable-identity lesson (f02426ff) for any new query-fed effect.

userStories.title: iOS: guided MeasureCard capture + native measurement overlay editor
userStories.description: As an iOS reseller (the primary capture device), the camera flow guides me to a good measurement shot — card fully visible, top-down, sharp — and I can review/adjust the extracted measurements natively, identical in behavior to the web editor.
acceptanceCriteria: Capture flow gains a skippable Measurement-shot step: live hint overlay (lay the MeasureCard beside the garment, all 4 squares visible); after capture the photo auto-tags photo_type=measurement and upload rides the existing foreground uploader

Post-upload, the app calls calibrate (+extract when the item has a garment class) and surfaces the quality-gate errors verbatim with a Retake affordance — a bad card shot is caught at the shelf, not at listing time
Native overlay editor mirrors the web editor: rectified image, draggable measurement lines, live inch values, amber low-confidence styling, identical save semantics via the same endpoints
Measurement photos are excluded from the iOS listing-photo picker/sync exactly like web (shared vocabulary)
iOS CI: unit tests for the px-to-inch math port and the photo-type exclusion; UI smoke for the editor sheet (no-ungated-print rule respected)
userStories.notes: iOS is not buildable on this Windows host — rides the iOS CI lane. Optional stretch ONLY if trivial: live card-visibility hint via Vision framework rectangle detection; full on-device detection is explicitly NOT required (server calibrate is the source of truth, keeping all platforms consistent).

userStories.title: Android: MeasureCard capture + measurement editor parity
userStories.description: As an Android reseller, I get the same guided measurement capture and overlay editor as iOS/web, backed by the same server-side calibrate/extract endpoints — no platform-specific CV.
acceptanceCriteria: Capture step with the same guidance + auto-tag photo_type=measurement; the Android photo-type enum gains measurement (the TODO hook from the vocabulary story)
Calibrate/extract calls + quality-error surfacing + Retake, matching iOS behavior
Compose overlay editor with draggable lines, live values, amber flags, identical save semantics
Measurement photos excluded from listing photo selection
Unit tests for the shared math port; runs in the Android CI lane once it exists (assembleDebug + testDebugUnitTest locally per the android-local-toolchain setup until then)
userStories.notes: DEPENDS on the Android client reaching photo-capture parity — keep pending until then rather than building against a moving target. All heavy lifting is server-side by design, so parity is UI-only.

userStories.title: Clean measurement-overlay listing asset: card-free annotated photo buyers can trust
userStories.description: As a reseller, GradeThread renders a clean, marketplace-safe measurements photo for my listing: the garment (card cropped OUT of frame) with unbranded measurement lines and inch labels burned in — the buyer-facing payoff of the whole system and a big listing-quality differentiator.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/flipdesk/measure/overlay {itemId}: renders from the rectified measurement photo — crop to the garment region EXCLUDING the card (the capture protocol guarantees the card sits beside the garment, so a deterministic crop removes it; NO inpainting in v1), then draw each saved measurement as a clean line with end-caps and an inch label (server-side ImageScript, same stack as the old badge compositor)
The rendered asset is UNBRANDED: plain lines + numbers only — no GradeThread logo, wordmark, URL, or QR (eBay third-party-marks / off-eBay-promotion policy; same rule family as the no-links pivot)

Asset stores as a generated item photo with a distinct type (e.g. measurement_overlay, added to the vocabulary surfaces like the measurement type), listing-ELIGIBLE but never auto-primary; regenerating after a measurement edit replaces the previous render
Composer/photo manager show it with an include-in-listing toggle (default ON when >= 2 measurements exist); publish + photo-sync append it after the seller's real photos

Graceful degradation: a crop that would clip the garment falls back to the full rectified frame with the card region masked to a flat background fill (not inpainting); if that also fails the overlay is simply skipped — publish is never blocked by overlay generation

Deno test: renderer draws the expected line/label count from a fixture measurement set; type-exclusion test that measurement stays OUT and measurement_overlay goes IN (non-primary) of the publish photo set
userStories.notes: This story answers the eBay concern: the CARD photo never ships (segregated by type), and the shipping overlay is card-free + brand-free. Annotated measurement photos are established eBay practice (Tailored's flagship output) — the policy risk is branding, not measurement callouts. BUILT 2026-07-03: migration 00350 (measurement_overlay enum) + version bump; vocabulary mirrored web/types/iOS; lib/measure-overlay.ts (invert homography -> card px bbox -> guillotine crop choosing the largest card-free side with a 35%-axis guard, mask-with-flat-fill fallback, thick halo lines + perpendicular end caps + label pills via ImageScript/Roboto — UNBRANDED, source-guard test); /extract now persists per-measurement LINE GEOMETRY additively into measure_calibration.lines (editor-corrected item.measurements value wins at render); POST /api/flipdesk/measure/overlay replaces the previous render, stores {ownerId}/{itemId}/measurement_overlay_*.jpg, trails sort_order, listing-eligible non-primary. DEVIATION: include-in-listing toggle = presence (delete/retag the generated photo to exclude) — a per-photo toggle column was not worth a second migration; revisit with US-1574 if sellers ask. Edge 2604/0.

userStories.title: Measurements ride every listing surface: eBay aspects + description block + cross-listing text
userStories.description: As a reseller, saved measurements should reach buyers everywhere automatically: eBay measurement item specifics, a formatted description block, the overlay photo, and plain-text lines on cross-listed platforms — one measurement pass, every surface.
acceptanceCriteria: eBay: the existing resolveMeasurementAspects/applyMeasurementsBlock paths consume the new measurements exactly as they do manual ones (regression tests updated to cover ai_measured-provenance values) — publish AND revise
Description block includes a one-line method note when measurements came from a calibrated photo (Measured flat via calibrated photo measurement) — text only, no URLs
Cross-listing generation (platform_fields variants) appends a plain-text measurements section per platform within each platform's description cap, using platform-appropriate unit formatting
Composer preview specifics + ListingKit measurement lines read the same store so the preview never disagrees with what publishes
AutoLister queue pre-flight surfaces a has-measurements informational badge (never blocking) on drafts, so batch reviewers see coverage at a glance
userStories.notes: Mostly wiring + tests: US-1450 already built the eBay fold-in; this story guarantees the new provenance and the overlay asset flow through publish, revise, AND the queue/bulk paths (watch the publish-time listings-row snapshot class of bug).

userStories.title: MeasureCard distribution: in-app ordering, printable download, fulfillment queue, version tracking
userStories.description: As a subscriber, I can get a MeasureCard: download the print-at-home PDF instantly, or request a professionally printed card mailed to me (plan-gated). As the operator, I get a fulfillment queue I can export to my print/mail vendor, and the system knows which card version each user has.
acceptanceCriteria: A MeasureCard page under FlipDesk settings/tools: what it is, capture do/donts, instant PDF download (the letter fallback), and Request-a-mailed-card for eligible plans

Mail request captures shipping address into a measure_card_requests table (US-1108-triple migration; deny-all operator table registered in rls-guard with owner_user_id) with status requested -> exported -> shipped; plan gating enforced server-side
Admin ops page lists + CSV-exports pending requests (address, plan, requested_at) and bulk-marks exported/shipped — the operator handles the actual print/mail vendor
A profile-side record tracks card_version delivered/downloaded so future card revisions can target upgrade messaging; calibrate already detects the version per photo from the marker ids
Education hook: one in-app announcement via the existing Growth broadcast system when the feature ships (draft copy included in the story; operator sends)
Abuse guard: one active mail request per user + rate limit on the request endpoint
userStories.notes: Fulfillment stays manual/vendor-side on purpose at this scale; the queue is just structured data. Shipping address is PII: operator table, service-role only, NEVER in item-photos or any public surface.

userStories.title: Measurement accuracy eval harness + correction telemetry (earning the word accurate)
userStories.description: As GradeThread, before we market photo measurements as accurate we need to KNOW the error distribution: a golden set of tape-measured garments the pipeline runs against on demand, plus production telemetry on how far users drag the auto lines — which doubles as training data for a future dedicated landmark model.
acceptanceCriteria: Golden set: >= 20 real garments across the class schema, each with operator tape-measured ground truth + a MeasureCard photo, stored as fixtures (photos in private storage, truth values in a JSON manifest)

An eval script (like the grading eval) runs calibrate+extract on the set and reports per-measurement error stats; RELEASE GATE for accuracy marketing: p50 <= 0.25in AND p95 <= 0.5in vs tape truth — until met, all UI copy says estimated from photo, review before listing

Production telemetry: on editor save, log the per-measurement delta between the ai_measured proposal and the final value (PostHog event + a compact measure_corrections operator table via migration) — deltas/class/confidence only, no photo content
An admin view (or documented SQL) surfaces the correction-delta distribution per garment class so we can see which measurements the auto pass gets wrong
Documented threshold review: when 30 days of telemetry shows p95 <= 0.5in for a class, that class's copy may drop estimated (a recorded human decision, not automatic)
userStories.notes: Same philosophy as the grading golden set: never claim accuracy you have not measured. The correction telemetry is also the labeled dataset that would let a Phase-3 trained landmark model (HRNet-style) replace the VLM-propose step if volume justifies it.

userStories.title: AI-action metering: one reserve/refund contract on EVERY model call + coverage drift test
userStories.description: As the operator, every Anthropic call a user triggers must count against their monthly AI-action allotment through ONE enforcement point. An audit (2026-07-03) found the atomic reserve_ai_action contract is applied on all flipdesk-ai endpoints and AutoLister batch generation, but several vision flows leak: AutoLister classify-photos counts via the non-atomic increment_ai_actions but has NO cap check at all; verify-groups and the cover/item photo-QA passes use the deprecated checkQuota->increment flow (TOCTOU past the cap, and cover-QA has no cap check); flipdesk-listings' lazy cross-variant fill increments without a verified cap. This is why heavy AI use during listing intake can feel like it never counts.
acceptanceCriteria: A single shared helper (e.g. lib/ai-metering.ts: withAiAction(ownerId, fn) — resolve limit, reserve_ai_action atomically, run fn, refund_ai_action on throw) replaces every direct checkQuota->increment_ai_actions sequence; increment_ai_actions has no remaining callers on user-triggered paths and its deprecation is noted where it is defined
flipdesk-scout AI endpoints (all three checkQuota sites) reserve+refund through the helper — scout vision calls now count

AutoLister classify-photos, verify-groups, cover photo-QA, and item photo-QA reserve atomically (cap-aware) instead of increment-after; multi-photo QA batches document their action granularity (one action per QA call, matching today's meter)
flipdesk-listings lazy generatePlatformVariants fill reserves before the model call

Documented + tested policy for BUNDLED sub-passes: one reserved action per generated item covers generation's internal tag-OCR/research-ID/verification/synthesis/aspect-extract sub-calls (today's behavior, now asserted by a test so it cannot silently double-bill)

Deliberately UNMETERED model calls are allow-listed with rationale in one place: grading pipeline + authenticity (billed via grade credits), support assistant (operator cost), admin/ops tooling — the allow-list is code, not tribal knowledge

COVERAGE DRIFT TEST: a static test walks services/edge-functions/src for imports of the model-calling libs (ai-config/callClaude consumers) and asserts every consuming route module either uses the metering helper or appears on the allow-list — a future AI feature that forgets metering fails CI (same drift-test pattern as rls-guard/cron-registry)
Billing page usage card is verified against a real flow in a test: one metered action moves usage.ai_actions_used_this_month by exactly 1 (and a failed model call refunds it)
userStories.notes: User-observed (2026-07-03): 'when I do listings and leverage AI it does not count against my allotment.' Two compounding causes: (a) the leaks above — intake-time photo roles/QA/group-verify are exactly the flows a heavy lister touches (scout, on closer read, already metered atomically via raw rpc calls — now unified on the lib helpers); (b) operator accounts are super_admin (plan-feature gates bypass) on a high-cap plan, so even metered actions barely dent the number. Do NOT add a super_admin quota bypass — operators should see real counts. AI_ACTION_LIMITS: free 25 / starter 200 / pro 750 / business 2000; reserve_ai_action is migration 00087.
